details:
MissionForge is an interactive browser-based space mission design and simulation game developed by Team Shade Drift. It allows users to create a complete mission by selecting a destination, spacecraft platform, scientific instruments, power system, communications system, propulsion, onboard autonomy, launch vehicle, and mission trajectory.

As users make choices, the game continuously evaluates engineering trade-offs involving budget, spacecraft mass, power consumption, data capacity, payload limits, scientific value, reliability, and mission risk. After the design is complete, MissionForge simulates major mission phases such as launch, cruise, arrival, science operations, and data return. Players then receive a mission score, engineering feedback, warnings, and recommendations for improving their design.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and runs entirely in a web browser through GitHub Pages. No installation or backend server is required.

Our goal is to make systems engineering and space mission planning easier for students to understand. Instead of learning mission trade-offs only through theory, users can experiment with different designs and immediately see how one decision affects the rest of the mission.

We focused on making the project educational, interactive, visually engaging, and simple enough for students to use while still representing important concepts found in real space mission planning.
